rule: Every resolved place remains selectable with its canonical score; only independently worthwhile settlements scoring 60 or more appear as town markers. Attractions never inflate settlement scores.
namingDecisions: Deebank and Strachan already exist and are not duplicated.
Arbeadie is retained as a historical locality absorbed into Banchory and remains distinct from Woodside of Arbeadie.
Belts of Collanach is corrected to Belts of Collonach.
East Mains resolves to the Banchory-area hamlet, not the South Lanarkshire namesake.

additions.rationale: Kincardine O'Neil and surrounding Deeside attractions remain separately assessed and do not inflate Tillydrine.
Banchory, Inchmarlo and nearby heritage remain separately bounded; their facilities are not transferred into Brathens.
The Trustach hills and informal countryside routes are not assumed to be visitor facilities or public attractions for the locality.
The bridge and countryside setting identify the hamlet, but Banchory and Inchmarlo services are not borrowed into its score.
This resolves to East Mains near Banchory and Brathens, not the South Lanarkshire namesake. Banchory attractions and facilities remain with Banchory.
Council evidence says Banchory amalgamated Arbeadie and Upper Arbeadie in the 1800s. This reference entry is distinct from Woodside of Arbeadie and cannot duplicate Banchory’s visitor offer.
Scolty Hill and Banchory remain separate visitor propositions. Their appeal does not promote Auchattie as a destination.
The requested spelling is corrected to Collonach. Strachan, Scolty and nearby archaeology remain separately assessed rather than transferred into this settlement score.
The requested spelling is normalised to Tillygarmond. Finzean Estate and wider Birse attractions are separate and do not create a town score here.
